data.name: Failure policy: no limit ends a run

lines:
# Failure policy - NO HARD LIMITS, report everything

Mandatory for every implementation task in this project:

1. NEVER make a limit terminate a run. No cap on model turns, tool calls, provider retries, recoveries, notices, retries, bytes, tokens, counters or elapsed work may end an Agent node. Limits and budgets are telemetry; they may size a message, never stop the work.
2. EVERY error is reported to the LLM and the run continues: provider, transport, contract, context preparation, request validation, tool invocation, tool settlement, commit. Report it, then keep going.
3. Exactly three conditions may end an Agent node: the model returned its final answer, the user cancelled, or an authority denied the call unrecoverably. Nothing else.
4. A bound may only shape what the model is told. Truncate with an explicit omitted count and say how to get the rest (e.g. job_list). Never fail a request because a notice grew.
5. Structural validation has two roles: an editor validator may reject and explain; the dispatch path must degrade (bound, truncate, drop the advisory field) because a rejected dispatch is a dead run.
6. Never write `return Err(...)` / `?` on a context-preparation, notice, budget or validation condition in the model/tool loop. If you find one, convert it to a reported notice.

Design authority: aworkit.workflow_worker.failure_policy (normative). A fatal return on any of these conditions is a design violation, not a provider error. Incident: chat.e1608e3b0f642edccf7dcb59588deb2a61dbd0fb ended after 61 minutes because a 5291-byte job notice crossed a 4 KiB request validation limit.
